t.4.33.1: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa, that bull among men, enraged and unchecked, enter, Sugrīva became agitated in all his senses.
t.4.33.2: Seeing that son of Daśaratha, enraged and sighing heavily, seeming to blaze with fiery energy, tormented by his brother's misfortune,
t.4.33.3: The best of monkeys sprang up, leaving his golden seat, like the great, well-adorned banner of Mahendra.
t.4.33.4: As Sugrīva sprang up, the women headed by Rumā leapt up after him, like hosts of stars following the full moon in the sky.
t.4.33.5: His eyes reddened, the glorious one swayed, his palms joined in reverence, and he stood there like a great wish-fulfilling tree.
t.4.33.7: A king who is endowed with strength of character and noble birth, who is compassionate, who has conquered his senses, who is grateful and who speaks the truth is honoured in the world.
t.4.33.6: Enraged, Lakṣmaṇa spoke to Sugrīva, who stood with Rumā as his companion in the midst of the women, like the moon accompanied by the stars.
t.4.33.8: But the king who, standing in unrighteousness, makes false his promise to friends who have helped him, who is more cruel than he?
t.4.33.9: By a falsehood concerning a horse a man slays a hundred, and by a falsehood concerning a cow a thousand; but by a falsehood concerning a man, a man destroys himself and his own kin.
t.4.33.11: This verse, revered by all the worlds, was sung by an angered Brahmā upon seeing an ungrateful man; learn it, O monkey.
t.4.33.10: He who, having first had his purpose accomplished by his friends, does not repay them in return is an ingrate and deserves to be slain by all beings, O lord of the monkeys.
t.4.33.12: For the slayer of a brahmin, for the drinker of liquor, for the thief, and likewise for one who has broken his vow, the virtuous have prescribed atonement; but for the ungrateful there is no atonement.
t.4.33.13: You are ignoble, ungrateful and a liar, O monkey, since, though your purpose was accomplished first by Rāma, you do not repay Rāma in return.
t.4.33.14: Surely, O monkey, you whose aim has been fulfilled, wishing to repay the service done for you, ought to make an effort in the search for Rāma's Sītā.
t.4.33.16: Sinful and evil-minded as you are, you were made to attain the kingship of the monkeys by the illustrious, great-souled Rāma, who knows compassion.
t.4.33.15: You, attached to vulgar pleasures and false to your promise, are such a one; Rāma does not know you for what you are, a serpent that croaks like a frog.
t.4.33.17: If you do not acknowledge the service done for you by Rāma, whose deeds are accomplished without strain, then you, struck down at once by sharpened arrows, will see Vālin.
t.4.33.18: The path by which Vālī went when he was slain has not narrowed. Keep to your pledge, Sugrīva, and do not follow the path of Vālī.
t.4.33.19: Surely you do not see the arrows, like thunderbolts, loosed from the bow of the foremost of the Ikṣvākus; that is why you, at ease, indulge in pleasure and do not give Rāma's task a thought even in your mind.
